P1.evidence: The four-part frame ran essentially complete: 'I just want to get a real picture of where you're at right now. What you're trying to get to, what's been stopping you and getting in the way. And if there's a way we can help you accomplish that, I can clearly show you how we can do it. If not, no worries.' Agreement was taken ('Sounds good? Sounds good.'). But there was no read-back of the setter's notes at all — Kyla is not mentioned once by the rep, and only surfaces at 01:29:53 when the prospect names her. The open question was never posed as such; the prospect simply started talking and the rep let him.

P2.evidence: Work was excavated properly — the rep reconstructed the actual day and corrected the prospect's own framing: 'you're not working from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. You're working from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.' Conditions and injuries were asked directly ('do you have any injuries or something like pains, chronic conditions?') and followed for duration and frequency ('That happens often?', 'how often does it, like every single day?'). Training week, results and energy all covered. Height was asked, weight and age volunteered. Diet was never asked — the rep conceded this himself at 00:43:39, 'I know we didn't cover that in depth', immediately before pitching the nutrition pillar. Sleep was never asked despite the prospect opening the call by saying he had been up all night with his son.

P3.evidence: The full surface-to-deep ladder ran, most of it close to verbatim. 'Outside of just the physical appearance and that you want to lose weight and get stronger, what's actually driving this for you right now?' then 'when we can get you to that point that you're feeling better ... what does that actually change in your life?' then 'who else does that impact also?' The chain landed on his children and then on the strongest image of the call — 'I'm the dad in the pool and the beach that keeps the shirt on' — which the rep pressed once more with 'how do you feel having to have a shirt when you're in the pool?' Reflect-back was sharp and accepted: 'from what I'm hearing, you've been sabotaging yourself' / 'I could agree with that.' Only P3c, a specific physical thing he cannot do, was left implicit.

P4.evidence: 'Why is that? Why have you been falling off?' and 'what's actually been stopping you ... what's been the biggest struggle?' produced the prospect's own diagnosis, and P4f ran in its strongest form: 'Let me ask you, why are we talking now and not a year ago?' returned 'I truly believed, and I say believed because that's no longer my belief, that this was something that I can do on my own.' The prospect then named the gap unaided — 'I need education. I need accountability and I need to know that I'm invested ... my wallet has to feel it too.' P4a is partial because prior programmes and coaches were never asked about; only his own unstructured attempts were covered.

P5.evidence: P5a ran and worked — 'if nothing changes actually, and we're sitting here, here from now, where does this go?' produced 'That would suck majorly. I'm not even sure how I would answer that ... I don't even want to think about this.' That is the moment the phase exists to create, and the rep did not stay in it: no 'why not?', and the settle-for question was asserted rather than asked ('I understand, like, you're not willing to settle for that'). 'Draw a line in the sand' was used, but as a statement during the money conversation ('right now we're at this situation again, where you need to draw a line in the sand and hold yourself to the fire') rather than as the commitment question.

P6.evidence: Both questions ran verbatim and before anything was presented. 'Do you believe you can actually get there if you had, like, the right structure, the right person in your corner?' — 'I believe I can get there.' Then 'if you had everything you needed, the program, the coach, the accountability that you mentioned is important for you, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' — 'No, no. If it checks off everything I'm looking for, then yes, I'd go in.' The rep confirmed the yes explicitly ('so 100% in') and re-took commitment after the pillars at 00:53:19. The preceding 'do you want information or do you actually want to change' / 'do you want or do you need to change' sequence is an unscripted but well-executed pre-commitment move.

P11.evidence: No programme purchase, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement email and the welcome/Skool steps were not reachable. The only transaction was a $100 refundable deposit to hold a follow-up slot, which is not a P11 step.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete OC execution in the batch. Isolation ran ('let's put finances on the side for a second ... is there anything else keeping you from being less than 100% sure'), the HOW reframe ran near-verbatim ('you're not in a, should I do it? It's more of a, how to pull it off place'), the upfront-versus-break-it-up line ran, permission was asked for ('if you were open to actually having an honest, open conversation about exactly how we could navigate around that'), and then five of the six financial-picture questions ran in order: cash on hand ($7,000), monthly surplus ($1,000-1,500), number of credit cards (three to four), available credit ($6,000), and investments (ruled out). Only used-versus-available was not separated out. The play was executed to the letter; what the letter produced was a plan to spend 43% of a joint emergency fund and the whole of the household's available credit.

Trigger was explicit and quantified: the wife's $2,000 ceiling. Nearly every scripted move ran — 'is there any reason Natalie would not want you to actually be stronger, like take off the shirt and like be confident', 'when you're going to talk with Natalie, how do you think she would actually react to this?', 'why would you put some of the responsibility on her?', 'let's say your Natalie is out of equation right now', and the fallback deposit ('put down a deposit, go talk to her, full refund if she says no'), which was executed literally at $100. The one scripted move that did not run is the one this prospect had pre-empted — 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' — and he is a mortgage loan officer who argued the opposite case himself. The rep also went off script with 'sometimes it's better to ask for forgiveness than for permission', which is not in the play and is recorded as a conduct flag.

Soft think-about-it trigger — 'I got to let my brain think a little bit, how I can make it happen. I think Monday, Monday I should have a clear idea.' Two OA-adjacent moves ran: the belief check had already been secured, and the delay was challenged once ('putting more time and delaying that ... it's getting you further and further away from the goal'). None of the sharp moves ran — no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', and no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?', all of which were available given the ten-year self-sabotage the prospect had just described.

Household-veto objection, not covered by the script. The blocker was not the prospect's belief, his capacity or his willingness — it was a jointly held budget with a specific number attached and a spouse who believes the goal should be achieved without paying anyone. The playbook's spouse play assumes an individual seeking permission for a personal bet; it has no path for jointly owned funds with an agreed cap, and it pushed the rep toward advising unilateral spending.

Undiagnosed active injury, not covered by the script. The prospect raised a knee that gives way and stated twice that he must see a doctor. There is no scripted move for pausing, conditioning the sale on clearance, or even documenting it, so the rep acknowledged it once ('okay, so that needs to be checked') and carried on selling. This is the same gap the playbook already records for clinical fit, and it appeared here as safety rather than programme fit.

notes: Process-wise the best call in the batch — the four-part frame, the full goals ladder, a real root-cause admission and both commitment questions before any number, followed by a by-the-book open-wallet. Two things to fix regardless of how Monday goes: the knee needs to become a gate, not a note, and the phase that was skipped is the one that would have done the work here — the prospect said 'that would suck majorly' about two more years of the same and the rep left it there instead of asking why not.
